macro_context: Mideast escalation (US-Iran conflict) pushed oil higher, triggering a global bond rout that India joined, with Asian equities (Kospi, Nikkei) down over 2% and the rupee sliding past 96/USD despite recent dollar-inflow measures - a broadly risk-off tape. Gold/silver firmed as a safe-haven/rate-hike-fear hedge. Partially offsetting: $2.5B of FII buying is fueling debate on whether foreign flows are structurally rotating into India. HDFC Bank's MD flagged El-Nino/below-normal-monsoon risk to FY27 growth and inflation. Q1 FY27 bank earnings season opens this week (HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Axis Bank, Kotak, Yes Bank, SBI, RIL among ~70 reporters) - the dominant near-term catalyst window.

names_in_play.catalyst: Goldman Sachs names it among 14 bullish stock picks (tier_A); ICICI Securities reiterates Buy, target Rs 1850 (tier_B). Q1 FY27 earnings due this week is the key event-risk window for the existing holding - thesis intact, no contradicting tier-A/B evidence.
Flagged among top Q1-earnings-week analyst picks alongside HDFC, Axis, Kotak, Yes Bank (tier_A). Results due this week; remains the priority watchlist name for the next open bank-sector-cap slot.

KR Choksey issues Accumulate, target Rs 1531 (tier_B). IT sector broadly firm today (TCS +6%, Infosys +3%) on TCS's AI-revenue beat and ABB deal win, but that IT-pop evidence is tier_C only - INFY's TCS read-through stays unconfirmed pending stronger sourcing.

Existing holding. Jefferies view surfaces 13% loan CAGR / 14% ROE and a $500M 5-yr bond, and shares are up 4.2% this week (both tier_C only - attention signal, not thesis-grade). Today's oil-driven bond rout and rupee weakness are a fresh headwind for PSU banks via G-sec MTM risk; no tier-A/B catalyst to upgrade conviction, watch the 1019 intraday tripwire.

macro_themes: Oil-driven bond rout and rupee weakness (risk-off) versus a $2.5B FII-inflow debate on India rotation
Q1 FY27 bank earnings season opens this week - key catalyst window for HDFCBANK, ICICIBANK, SBIN
El-Nino/below-normal-monsoon risk to the FY27 growth-inflation outlook
